title: Address postalCode field renamed to postcode in the Account API
query: What breaks across repositories if the address JSON field postalCode is renamed to postcode in Account's address API?

affected_repositories.name: account-service
affected_repositories.evidence_note: Owns the field. api/dto/AddressRequest.java, api/dto/AddressResponse.java, domain/model/Address.java, infrastructure/persistence/row/AddressRow.java, application/AddressBookService.java, api/AddressController.java, mybatis/mapper/AddressMapper.xml, db/migration/V1__identity_schema.sql, and the generated openapi/account.yaml.

affected_repositories.name: order-service
affected_repositories.evidence_note: infrastructure/client/AccountClient.java declares record AddressResponse(..., String postalCode, ...) and reads response.postalCode() when building the quote address snapshot. After the rename Jackson binds null, so the quote and the resulting order carry a null postcode. Fails silently at runtime, not at compile time.

affected_repositories.name: commerce-web
affected_repositories.evidence_note: src/api/types.ts declares postalCode on the address type; src/pages/CheckoutPage.tsx renders it at line 112 and binds the input at line 119.

notes:
Derived from the built estate, not from the design table. Design section 22 predicts Account, BFF, Order, Shipment, SPA; two of those are false positives and are excluded deliberately.

EXCLUDED - commerce-bff. Zero postalCode references in src/main. api/AddressProxyController.java relays com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode and never names a field, so the rename passes through with no compile break, no runtime break, and no code change. An untyped pass-through BFF is genuinely outside the blast radius of a field rename.

EXCLUDED - shipment-service. Twelve files match a naive grep for postalCode, and none belong to the contract being changed. infrastructure/messaging/OrderConfirmedListener.java reads address.path("postalCode") from order.confirmed.v1, whose payload is produced by order-service and frozen in wave1-shared-contracts.md; order keeps emitting postalCode because its own event contract does not change. api/dto/DeliveryEstimateRequest.java declares shipment's own request field, and order-service passes it a scalar via ShipmentClient Map.of("postalCode", postalCode, ...). This is the discriminating case in the corpus: a true negative that looks like a strong positive to any tool matching on identifier text.

COVERAGE GAP - order-service has the most severe impact and no test that detects it. No test exercises AccountClient over HTTP; there is no WireMock or MockRestServiceServer in order-service/src/test, and every test substitutes FakeAccountPort. Only the platform e2e flow surfaces the break.
